findings.evidence: Spec requirement 'The Claude writer credential is scoped to the writer process' says 'The token file location SHALL be read-denied inside the sandbox.' In template/scripts/sandboxed_writer.py, build_profile builds deny_read from DENY_READ_HOME, protected and platform only. launch_sandboxed_writer never passes the token path. A token_file outside ~/.config/dev-platform (for example ~/secrets/claude-token) stays readable to the writer. No test covers this.
findings.summary: The spec requires the token file location to be read-denied inside the sandbox. build_profile only denies a fixed home list, and nothing adds the configured token_file path to denyRead.

findings.evidence: srt_launcher returns ['npx','--yes','@anthropic-ai/sandbox-runtime@0.0.79']. launch_sandboxed_writer passes it through run_llm(command, checkout, ...), which uses cwd=checkout, and the operator OAuth token is in that process environment. The design's alternative of a resolvable `srt` binary with a matching --version is not implemented.
findings.summary: The pinned runtime is fetched and executed with `npx --yes` outside the sandbox. It runs with cwd set to the writer checkout, so a repository .npmrc or similar npm config there can influence the launcher. There is no integrity check on the fetched package.

findings.evidence: The proposal lists 'the push remote path when local' among the denyWrite paths. build_profile accepts extra_deny_write, but launch_sandboxed_writer never passes it and has no parameter for it. Only the unit tests use extra_deny_write.
findings.summary: The proposal says the profile denies writes to the push remote path when it is local. launch_sandboxed_writer has no way to supply it, so a local-path remote stays writable if it lies in an allowed root and is unprotected.

findings.evidence: template/scripts/sandboxed_writer.py, last lines of launch_sandboxed_writer: env={k: v for k, v in env.items() if k != TOKEN_ENV} with extra_env={TOKEN_ENV: token}, after sandboxed_env sets env[TOKEN_ENV]. SAFE_GIT is also duplicated from lifecycle_workers.
findings.summary: The writer environment is assembled in two places and the token is split off and re-added. sandboxed_env builds it and puts the token in, then the launcher strips the token and passes it again as extra_env. The two paths can drift.
